model: ResNet-50 ArcFace INT8 (static QDQ, per-channel weights)

quality_filter.note: Pairs excluded if either image's FaceQNet quality score is below the bottom-N% cutoff (computed on the full scored LFW population) or if SCRFD detection failed on that image. Filtering applied via the same None-cache-entry mechanism baseline_pipeline.py already uses for undetected faces -- lfw_10fold/compute_fairness_metrics unmodified.

latency.note: Original p95 (62.1ms vs 25.0ms median) diagnosed via onnxruntime profiling: NOT a warm-up artefact (measure_latency already discards 100 warm-up calls before timing) and NOT a periodic ORT-internal pattern (outlier gap distribution had no dominant period). Root cause: external system contention on this shared personal laptop (AMD Ryzen 7840HS, Balanced power plan, background RGB-sync processes ASUS Aura Sync + NZXT NGenuity polling for CPU cycles) -- confirmed because (1) FP32 showed a proportionally similar tail whenever contention was present, ruling out an INT8-specific kernel cause; (2) profiling of the slowest calls showed the excess wall-clock time was NOT attributable to any traced ORT op (sum of per-op durations was nearly identical between slow and median-speed calls) -- the extra time was lost between node executions, the signature of OS thread preemption, not slower compute; (3) three repeated clean re-measurements on 2026-09-11 all showed p95/median ratios of ~1.1-1.2x with no fat tail, vs the original run's 2.5x ratio. Latency figures above are the median of those 3 clean repeats (n_warmup=100, n_runs=1000 each, matching measure_latency() defaults). Recommend documenting in the dissertation that CPU latency benchmarks on this machine carry a system-contention caveat rather than presenting p95 as a precise, reproducible deployment figure.

latency_note: Reused from the unfiltered baseline run for this model -- latency is a per-inference model property independent of which pairs are included in the accuracy/fairness stats.
